title: I added zombies to my Half Life 2 x Black Ops 1 merger...
author: DeltaEchoX2
selftext:
For anyone interested in my earlier post whereby I merged Black Ops 1 (OG) gameplay systems into Half Life 2.. I added zombies into it. Zombies will forever spawn as long as there are combine soldiers alive in the level.

Additional changes:

* Added aim down sights
* Added a proper sprinting animation
* Added barrel flash when firing
* Added recoil
* Added more guns: China Lake, Crossbow, Famas
* Zombies mode on/off
   * When activated, plays the child laughing sound
   * When deactivated plays the "bye bye" soundbyte
* Fixed various weird bugs such as body collision was causing issues when zombies hitboxes wouldn't go when killed

replies.author: DeltaEchoX2
replies.body:
Ghidra to to decompile the game  
Opus 5.5 to generate the prompt + ported code. mine was:

>!You are helping me with a private, non-distributed modding project called "port bo1". The goal is to build a playable Half-Life 2 mod that uses Black Ops 1 single-player assets and recreates BO1's core gameplay feel (movement, shooting and everything in between) on top of the Source engine. The model I'm following is chasmlol/2010-rust-rewrite-mashup. All game files come from copies I own. ## What's on disk - HL2 / Source base: \[PATH\_TO\_SOURCE\_SDK\_2013\] (Source SDK 2013 singleplayer, the official open-source codebase) - HL2 game install: \[PATH\_TO\_HL2\_INSTALL\] - BO1 decomp (Ghidra + ReAgent output): \[PATH\_TO\_BO1\_DECOMP\] - BO1 game install / extracted assets: \[PATH\_TO\_BO1\_ASSETS\] - Working output folder for the mod: \[PATH\_TO\_MOD\_OUTPUT\] ## Ground rules 1. Use Source SDK 2013 as the engine and game code base. Use the HL2 decomp only when something isn't in the SDK. 2. Treat the BO1 decomp as a behaviour reference only. Read it to work out the tuning values, state machines and formulas (move speeds, sprint timings, ADS transitions, recoil patterns, spread, reload states, dolphin dive, prone, mantling and so on), then write a clean reimplementation in Source C++. Don't paste decompiled code into the SDK. 3. Before writing any code, explore both codebases and write PLAN.md covering: - The BO1 systems you found (function names/addresses in the decomp, what each one does, the key constants) - The matching Source classes (CGameMovement, CBasePlayer/CHL2\_Player, CBaseCombatWeapon/CWeaponHL2MPBase, viewmodel code, etc.) - A phased roadmap, with a clear "done" test for each phase Stop and wait for my approval once PLAN.md is written. 4. Set up git in the mod folder and commit at the end of every phase with a clear message. 5. Keep a running NOTES.md with decomp findings (addresses, constants, open questions) so we don't redo work. 6. When something is uncertain (e.g. a constant that might be wrong), say so and give me a test to check it in-game instead of guessing quietly. ## Phases (fine-tune these in PLAN.md) Phase 1: Build environment - Get Source SDK 2013 SP compiling as a standalone mod in \[PATH\_TO\_MOD\_OUTPUT\], with gameinfo.txt mounting HL2 content. Confirm it launches into a stock HL2 map. Phase 2: Asset pipeline (scripted and repeatable) - Write scripts in /tools that convert BO1 assets into Source formats: - Models (weapons, viewmodels/arms, characters): BO1 export, then Blender (SMD/DMX), then QC files, then studiomdl to .mdl - Textures: convert to .vtf and generate .vmt materials - Animations: viewmodel anims (idle, fire, reload, sprint, ADS) retargeted to Source sequences and activities - Sounds: weapon and footstep audio to .wav, plus soundscripts - Begin with ONE weapon end to end (e.g. the M16 or AK-74u) before batching the rest. - Log every converted asset in assets/manifest.csv (source file, output file, status, notes). Phase 3: Player movement - Recreate BO1 movement in a custom CGameMovement subclass: walk/sprint speeds and acceleration, sprint duration and recovery, crouch, prone, dolphin dive, mantling, jump height, fall behaviour, view bob and sway. - Make every tuning value a ConVar so I can tweak it live. Phase 4: Weapons - New weapon base class with ADS (FOV change, move-speed penalty, transition time), hipfire spread vs ADS spread, recoil patterns, sprint-to-fire delay, reload states (including reload cancel), weapon switch timings and damage falloff. - Data-drive each weapon through weapon scripts that hold the values pulled from the decomp. - Port the Phase 2 weapon in first, then the rest. Phase 5: HUD and feel - BO1-style crosshair that grows with spread, hitmarkers, ammo counter, damage indicators, plus any important camera effects (ADS blur, flinch). Phase 6: Test content - A small test map (or a modified HL2 map) to check movement and weapons, plus a short checklist I can run through. ## How to work - Do one phase at a time. At the end of each phase, give me a brief summary, the exact build/launch steps, and what I should test in-game. - Before installing a tool (Crowbar, VTFCmd, Blender add-ons, etc.), tell me what it is and why it's needed. - Don't change anything outside \[PATH\_TO\_MOD\_OUTPUT\] and /tools without asking first. Start by exploring the folders above and drafting PLAN.md.!<

  
from there it gave me a useable baseline.

From there I just had provide super basic and high-level changes to get it where it is today. Once the guns and movement had the right feel, I worked on the zombies implementation.

Usage/token-wise I used most of my session usage (pro plan) for about 3 - 5 sessions and about 20-30% of my weekly usage -- not bad really.
